transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-22 15:30 PT | Duration: 42m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Lena (Emerald Head of ML), Marcus (CTO), Sasha (Backend Lead), Jared (Product)

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick intros?
[00:05] Lena: Hi I'm Lena, Head of ML at Emerald, we run a small team and are looking to add LLM features to our analytics product.
[00:12] Marcus: Marcus here, CTO, mostly listening for infra/security implications.
[00:16] Maya: Awesome, Diego from our infra team will talk about perf and quickstart. Diego?
[00:21] Diego: Hey all, quick overview — Redwood offers hosted API for fastest time-to-value, Dedicated for predictability, and Private for VPC/on-prem. For PLG teams usually start hosted, redeem free credits, run quickstart to first token within minutes.
[00:40] Sasha: Quick question, when you say time-to-first-token, what does that mean in practice? cold start, SDK, latency?
[00:46] Diego: Good Q. Time-to-first-token has two parts: dev experience (curl/SDK + API key exchange) and runtime latency. With our quickstart you can be calling the API within 10-15 minutes, and typical p95 streaming latencies from us on hosted are sub-300ms for small prompts on curated models — but it depends on region and model.
[01:08] Jared: And the free credits — how does that work? trial length, token limits?
[01:12] Maya: We give an initial free credit package for quick evaluation — I'll send the exact redemption link after the call. Usually enough to run dev flows and a small benchmark.
[01:22] Marcus: What about data controls — we can't send PII to a hosted multi-tenant service for some customers.
[01:28] Diego: Totally — that's where Dedicated or Private comes in. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and isolation, plus retention policies. Private is for VPC or on-prem where you keep data inside your network. For quickstart we recommend hosted unless regulatory constraints block it.
[01:45] Lena: We're leaning hosted first to move fast but need to vet security: SOC2, SSO, RBAC, KMS integration for keys.
[01:54] Maya: We have SOC 2 Type II, SSO via SAML/OIDC, RBAC, and KMS integrations documented. I'll attach the security pack.
[02:05] Marcus: How does key management work if we want to use our KMS?
[02:09] Diego: You can use customer-managed keys with Dedicated or Private. For hosted we support envelope encryption and customer KMS via a managed integration in enterprise plans.
[02:19] Sasha: From an infra ops perspective, what does the SDK look like? Is there a hosted SDK and can we self-host later without changing a bunch of code?
[02:27] Diego: We try to keep the API consistent across environments. SDK calls are the same; you can pin model versions. Moving from hosted to Dedicated should be mostly config changes. Some provider names and endpoints differ, but the request interface is consistent.
[02:42] Lena: How about costs — we care about tokens per call and latency vs cost trade-offs.
[02:47] Maya: Redwood Optimize suggests batching/quantization profiles to balance cost and latency. For PLG quickstart we'll recommend a small batch config and cached prefixes to cut unit costs. We'll include cost-estimation guidelines in the doc we send.
[02:59] Marcus: Any competitors we should benchmark against?
[03:02] Diego: Customers often compare us to OpenAI and Anthropic for hosted APIs and to vendors like Cohere. We can include a benchmark spreadsheet if you want.
[03:12] Jared: For the perf test, can you run a 50k token run or some sample traces?
[03:16] Diego: Yep — we can run a short perf benchmark using your prompt set or our suggested prompts. It'll measure p50/p95 latencies and token cost.
[03:25] Lena: Our timeline is tight: we'd like to have a POC by early May, possibly expand to Dedicated in June if numbers look good.
[03:32] Maya: That sounds reasonable. We'll aim to get you credits and bench results within the next week.
[03:37] Sasha: A couple of nitty-gritty items — does Redwood provide audit logs for request/response metadata without content? We need tamper-evident logs for compliance.
[03:47] Diego: Yes, audit logs and trace hooks are part of Redwood Console. You can configure retention and integrate with SIEM. Full request/response content logging is optional and should be gated for compliance.
[03:59] Marcus: Any requirements for VPC peering or network egress if we go Private?
[04:04] Diego: For Private deployments we offer VPC options and can do peering or private link. For on-prem we do a packaged appliance. We'll follow up with network diagrams.
[04:16] Lena: Great. Also would like to see an example of the quickstart code path — how to get a token, sample curl, and how to stream results.
[04:25] Diego: I'll share SDK snippets and a demo curl. Typical quickstart flow: sign up, redeem credits, create API key, run sample prompt, examine latency and costs.
[04:36] Jared: Any gotchas with rate limits during the trial?
[04:40] Maya: Trial has reasonable default rate limits; we can bump them for a short benchmarking window. If you plan high throughput testing we can open a burst window.
[04:50] Marcus: Security review — do you have a customer security questionnaire or an ATO pack?
[04:54] Maya: Yes, we have a security questionnaire and SOC2 pack. I'll send both; Diego will help answer any technical Qs.
[05:06] Lena: On pilot scope — we'd like to validate: 1) dev experience (time-to-first-token), 2) latency at p95 for our key prompts, 3) cost estimates for our production load.
[05:16] Diego: Sounds good. For time-to-first-token we can instrument the SDK and measure from key creation to first streamed token; typically under 15 minutes for a dev.
[05:25] Sasha: Can the quickstart include a small sample webhook integration to show streaming into our app?
[05:30] Diego: Yep, we have example webhooks and streaming SDK examples.
[05:35] Maya: To recap next steps — I'll send quickstart + credits + security pack; Diego will run benchmark and send sample curl/SDK; Lena will send prompts and compliance notes. Plan to reconvene after benchmark.
[05:47] Marcus: OK thanks all.
[05:50] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up.

Notes: transcript contains a few autogenerated mislabels, some words transcribed phonetically (e.g., KMS sometimes shows as K-M-S), occasional false punctuation.
footer_notes: Call ended with clear next steps: send docs, run perf benchmark, confirm pilot scope. Transcript export may have minor errors typical of automated transcription.
